chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdul Rahman al-Muqarri narrated that Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Muqarri al-Gorjany quoted Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Mooseli in Baghdad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Asim al-Tarifi, on the authority of Abu Zayd Ayash ibn Zayd ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kihal - the servant of Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of Zayd ibn al-Hassan, on the authority of Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father as-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), who said:

People are in four groups: an ignorant person who is ruined and embraces his whims; a worshipper who is haughty, and as he increases in worship, he increases in pride; a scholar who wants his heels to be trodden upon (to be followed) and loves the praise of people; and a knowledgeable person on the path of truth who loves to uphold it but is either unable or overpowered. This one is the best of your contemporaries and the most sound in intellect.
ai.seo_question: What are the four types of people according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this classification in *Al-Khisal* to illustrate the spiritual pitfalls of the three lower classes—specifically the pride of the worshipper (*al-'abd al-mutaqawwi*) and the vanity of the scholar seeking human praise—contrasting them with the *'arif* who embodies humility despite power. This hadith is central to Shia gnosis (*'irfan*), emphasizing that true wisdom lies not merely in ritual or knowledge, but in the sincere pursuit of the Truth (*Haqq*) while remaining free from the ego's desire for status.
